title: Control plane boundary matrix and multi-region routing notes
body:
Purpose:
Quick working draft to (1) propose a compact ownership matrix for the control plane service boundaries, (2) define how routing policies should be partitioned between the API gateway, orchestration layer, and runtime adapters, and (3) capture multi-region constraints we must bake into the policies and adapters. This is intentionally pragmatic — we want clear handoffs so teams can move fast without ambiguity.

Summary / TL;DR:
- API Gateway: front-line policy enforcement (auth, per-tenant rate-limits, coarse routing by tier/region), light-weight routing decisions (region affinitized, emergency fallback).
- Orchestration: placement, rollout/traffic-shift policies, autoscaling decisions, capacity-aware routing hints, persistent policy store and audit trail.
- Runtime Adapters (serving-runtime): model-variant selection, kernel/quantization mapping, hot KV/prefix cache decisions and last-mile fallbacks when a model variant is unavailable.
- Multi-region: prefer region-affinity at gateway, region-aware capacity signals from orchestration, and consistent fallback semantics across regions at the adapter.

Design goals and constraints (constraints first):
- Low-latency decision path: keep per-request critical path small in the gateway; heavy policy evaluation should be precomputed or cached.
- Clear ownership: each decision must have an owning team and an eventing contract so the others can subscribe to policy changes.
- Fail-open predictable behavior: define safe defaults when the policy store or orchestration is unreachable.
- Auditability: every routing/placement decision needs traceable context (tenant, route, policy version, decision rationale).
- Compatibility with Dedicated/Private deployments: separation between control plane and data plane that works across hosted and air-gapped environments.

Ownership matrix (proposed):
- API Gateway (owner: eng-platform-engineering): auth, JWT validation, tenant identification, request throttling, request shaping, first-pass routing (region choice, top-level model family selection), applying customer-specified network ACLs, returning structured error codes for control-plane initiated fallbacks.
- Orchestration (owner: eng-platform-engineering): policy store, rollout engine (canary/A-B/gradual), autoscaler, placement decisions (region/pool), traffic shifting orchestration, capacity accounting, global live view and audit logs.
- Serving Runtime / Runtime Adapters (owner: engineering/serving-runtime): last-mile decisioning (exact model binary variant, quantization profile, kernel selection), prefix/KV cache warming, per-request KV cache lookup, latency-SLO enforcement at the worker level, adapter-side fallback strategies (downgrade quantization, use smaller model variant), metrics emission for decision telemetry.
- Console / Rollouts UI (owner: product-console): the UX for configuring rollouts, viewing policy diffs, and approving large shifts.
- Private Deployments (owner: eng-private-deployments): offer local policy store adapters, KMS integrations, and control-plane connectors for air-gapped customers.

Routing policy decomposition (who decides what and when):
1) Gateway-level (fastpath, synchronous on request):
   - Tenant / API key mapping (gateway)
   - Region affinity (gateway, based on region cookie / geo IP / client hint)
   - Tier-level routing: direct high-tier customers to reserved pools (gateway consults a cached partition table)
   - Emergency fallback: switch to pre-configured fallback model family when orchestration is unavailable
2) Orchestration-level (event-driven, cached policies):
   - Placement and pool selection policy (region/pool assignment per tenant/model)
   - Canary and rollout rules (percentage windows, time windows, dependency constraints)
   - Autoscaling policies and burst capacity allocation (decide when to enable shared overflow pools)
   - Cost-aware routing hints (mark model variants as high-cost and annotate routing weight)
3) Runtime Adapter-level (worker-local, last-mile):
   - Model variant selection for a specific request (hot/best-effort decisions)
   - Kernel and quantization choice based on sequence length hints and adapter telemetry
   - Local cache/eviction policy, eviction-triggered fallback (e.g., recompile lower-precision variant)
   - Fallback ordering and retry semantics (how many retries, backoff, degrade to smaller model)

Multi-region specifics to embed in the policies:
- Data residency: cluster-level tenancy flags in policy store to ensure requests flagged for a region never cross into an unintended region. Gateway must apply a hard deny if a tenant requires strict residency and orchestration suggests cross-region placement.
- Region-aware SLOs: a tenant can specify per-region latency SLOs. Orchestration must surface pool candidates that meet those SLOs; runtime adapters should log and surface violations.
- Failover semantics: decide between synchronous failover (gateway re-routes to another region) vs asynchronous (queue and retry). Default: synchronous only for read-heavy or idempotent workloads; write/consistency-sensitive flows must be rejected unless explicit cross-region consent is given.
- Cache coherence: prefix/KV caches are region-scoped. For global cache entries (e.g., public prompt cache), we must include TTL + origin tags and a version vector in the policy so adapters can validate freshness.

Policy versioning and rollout behavior:
- Policies stored in orchestration are versioned (semantic version + monotonic sequence).
- Gateway keeps a cache of the active policy version and subscribes to change events. On policy mismatch the gateway should log and continue with cached policy for up to 60s, then failover to safe defaults.
- Runtime adapters include the active policy version in trace spans so post-hoc analysis can attribute decisions to policy versions.

Security and compliance obligations that affect boundaries:
- Authn/Authz: gateway handles primary auth; for delegated auth (private deployments or offline tokens) runtime adapter must be able to validate signed assertions from gateway.
- KMS/HSM: private deployments have owner responsibilities to integrate KMS; orchestration provides pointer metadata to the runtime rather than keys.
- Audit logs: orchestration retains a copy of routing decisions (tenant, request id, chosen pool/model, policy version) for 90 days by default; export hooks to long-term storage are available as an add-on.

Operational runbook snippets (for quick use by SRE/Support):
- If a region shows high 5xxs: check orchestration capacity metrics -> if capacity shows healthy but latency high, inspect adapter-level fallbacks and kernel recompile failures.
- If gateway policy cache is stale: force policy refresh and compare policy versions between gateway and orchestration; check event subscription backlog.
- If a tenant reports cross-region leakage: run tenant policy query and the audit trace for last 100 requests; prioritize the hard-deny data residency check.

Open questions / decisions to take in the next design review:
- Should the gateway ever perform cost-aware routing decisions (cost vs latency tradeoff) or should it only follow orchestration hints? Proposal: gateway should only use cost hints as secondary signals to prefer cheaper compatible pools only for non-SLO-critical requests.
- Exactly how much policy logic is acceptable in the gateway without violating low-latency constraint? We need empirical thresholds (e.g., <200us added latency).
- Fallback ordering: define explicit global default ordering (e.g., same-pool smaller-variant -> cross-pool same-region -> cross-region) vs per-tenant overrides.
- How to surface model-compatibility metadata (quantization/compiled kernels) in a compact protocol so adapters can choose without heavy RTTs.

Concrete next steps / action items:
- Platform-eng to codify the ownership matrix in the team RACI doc and add the event contracts (RDINF-1423) — owner: Maya; due: 2024-11-20.
- Orchestration team to prototype a policy diff API that returns candidate pools with cost/latency annotations — owner: Arjun; prototype by 2024-12-08.
- Serving-runtime to define adapter protocol v0.1 (metadata fields, fallback semantics, trace tags) and a small test harness for cross-region fallbacks — owner: Liam; ship draft: 2025-01-12.
- Console/product to mock the rollout UX that exposes policy version and audit timeline for a tenant — owner: Sofia; demo: 2025-01-30.

Notes to self / collaboration cues (informal):
- This should be distributed as a short read before the architecture sync. Keep the doc intentionally terse — we'll add sequence diagrams in the next pass.
- Ping SRE for disaster exercises focused on region cutover and audit retention quotas.
- Pull sample telemetry for model-variant fallbacks — I suspect we recompile/timeout on long-form requests more often in eu-west-1.

References and related docs:
- control-plane-reference-sketch (Confluence)
- RDINF-1423 (ownership RFC stub)
- platform/policy-store design PR #981 (link above)

End.
